Question: In cricket, how is a winner decided when both teams have scored the same number of runs and wickets are equal?
Answer: Some possibilities for how a winner can be decided in cricket when both teams have scored the same number of runs and wickets are equal :- •Draw - If the match is a Test match, the match will continue until one team has won. If the match is still tied at the end of the scheduled number of days, the match will be declared a draw and the teams will share the points. •Tie - A tie is a more common result, as the matches are much longer and there is more scope for weather interruptions. If the match is ODI or T20I, the match will go to a Super Over. The team that scores the most runs in the Super Over will win the match. If the Super Over also ends in a tie, the match will be declared a tie and the teams will share the points. •Bowl-Out - the winner can be decided by a bowl-out. A bowl-out is a competition between the two teams' bowlers, with each bowler attempting to bowl three deliveries that are as close to the stumps as possible. The team with the most wickets at the end of the bowl-out wins the match. •No Result - A no result is declared when a limited overs cricket match cannot be completed due to weather or light interruptions. This means that neither team can be declared the winner, and the match is effectively drawn. If the weather or light stops the game before each team has batted for the minimum number of overs, the match is declared a no result. •Abandoned - A cricket match can be abandoned if the weather or other conditions prevent any play from occurring at all. If the bowler of the first over of play has not started his/her runup when the officials decide to abandon play, the match is termed 'abandoned without a ball being bowled'. Question: It was Sunday on Jan 1, 2006. What was the day of the week Jan 1, 2011?

The extra 1 day is the day from the leap year 2008, it is the only leap year to lie between 2006–2011) = 1826 Now dividing 1826 with 7 ( 7 days of a week), we get 260 + 6 Here, 6 is the remainder days. Given that, Jan 1, 2006 is a Sunday. Now we add 6 days to Sunday we get Saturday, which is the day of the week Jan 1, 2011

Question: What is a black hole?
Answer: A black hole forms when a large, dying star collapses. The gravity created by this condensing matter completely overpowers any outward forces, including light. Although a black hole emits no light, its presence is detectable by radioastronomy equipment. Question: How does fracking work?
Answer: Fracking uses a high pressure injection of water, sand, and chemicals to break open subterranean shale and hold the newly formed fissures open so that oil and gas can seep to the wellhead and be pumped to the surface. It's a process that has been used in around traditional wells for decades as a way to coax more production from the reservoir. In combination with horizontal drilling, however, it has allowed access to vast quantities of previously inaccessible oil and natural gas. The pipe used for oil and production are stiff in individual sections, but once thousands of feet of pipes are strung together, they can bend a full 90 degrees. As a result, a wellbore can be turned in any direction and pushed through rock formation. Advances in fracking technology allow engineers to steer the drill more precisely and sense the chemical properties of the surrounding rock. Oil field engineers can then home in on petroleum-rich seams. Image Source : Google
